About

Fusion Updates (fusionupdates.com) turns Oracle's quarterly readiness documentation into a filterable, plain-English list of changes across Oracle Fusion Cloud, with impact ratings and a what-to-test checklist for every update.

Get the 26D checklist now: what switches on by itself, which former opt-ins are now standard, what to test

Inside the free 26D checklist (PDF):

  • The 23 opt-ins Oracle lists as ending with 26D: 9 switch on for everyone, 14 need setup
  • 9 HCM Redwood default switches and other HCM notices for 26D
  • 9 baseline regression checks, plus typical 26D test and production dates by cohort

Then one plain-English email per Oracle quarterly update, linked to Oracle's docs. Free. 4 emails a year plus short opt-in alerts. Unsubscribe anytime. Read issue #1 (26C) → · Privacy

It is run by an experienced Oracle consultant. Every entry links back to its Oracle source page. Summaries are condensed from Oracle's text, and impact-on-upgrade ratings are editorial judgment, so always check the Oracle page and your own configuration.

This is an independent site, not affiliated with or endorsed by Oracle.

Two labels per feature: Impact on upgrade is our rating of what changes for existing users on update day, with nobody acting. Oracle scale is Oracle's own size rating ("Larger scale" or "Small scale", from its "Impact to Existing Processes" column), shown only when Oracle gives one.

Method: features come from the "Feature Summary" tables in Oracle's What's New documents. Enablement comes from Oracle's "Action to Enable" column plus the Current Opt-In Expirations list. Impact on upgrade: high means users have to change how they work, or it's a large UI or process change, a former opt-in that becomes standard and affects users, or it touches payments, accounting, integrations or security. Medium means visible but contained, or switched on automatically and noticeable. Low means minor, cosmetic, reporting-only, or it needs setup before anyone gets it. Each rating is checked against Oracle's feature page (description, action to enable, scale and opt-in status).
